title: What the status endpoint reports
response:
the header every endpoint carries, plus the server's own version and sizes

HTTP 200 OK
{
  "dbSize": "28672",
  "dbSizeInUse": "28672",
  "dbSizeQuota": "2147483648",
  "downgradeInfo": {},
  "header": {
    "cluster_id": "7259173788625807763",
    "member_id": "14791908393849053773",
    "raft_term": "2",
    "revision": "1"
  },
  "leader": "14791908393849053773",
  "raftAppliedIndex": "4",
  "raftIndex": "4",
  "raftTerm": "2",
  "storageVersion": "3.7.0",
  "version": "3.7.1"
}
note: The revision in the header is the store's clock and is at least 1 on an empty store, because bringing the cluster up is itself a write. member_id identifies the server that answered and is never zero.

title: An endpoint that is not there
note: A catch-all that answers 200 with an empty body is the trap: every decoder in this suite reads a missing field as its zero, so an empty 200 looks exactly like a successful request that found nothing.
